title: Sacko and Ina Ray Hutton on the Ellington show
summary: Green says dancers brought a thrilling tumbling jazz tap called sacko, and tells of Patterson and Jackson replacing the Berry Brothers and Ina Ray Hutton singing.

bands.name: Ina Ray Hutton and Her Orchestra

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: But the dancers done all right. They introduced sacko -- they brought that to the profession. Called sacko -- that's handling it down from tap dancing -- sacko.
thrilling -- it's like exciting, very exciting and, you know, it's suspenseful like that.
Is it a type of tap dance?
Oh, (unintelligible). It's like a shape -- it's like a shape -- sacko -- they wouldn't do that -- that couldn't be done, you know. It's that kind of, you know --

Oh, if this place was a little larger, I could, you see, I would be glad to, you see. I'm just trying to explain it. See, these are the things that are to remain, you know, in the world -- in history, you see. Because they were discoveries, you see, and they were being fostered constantly by the general public, you see. And there was -- you know, there was quite a bit -- abdication was kind of famous too, you see. That's the royal households, you know. Like they would be here in America. And eventually they would go back -- they would leave or go somewhere's else. But I mean they would always -- they had someting to take with them, in other words. They had great memories -- something to do -- something better to do when they got out of exile -- got back to, you know. So, we went from there, from Penn (Laughter) theater -- this is the (unintelligible) tour with Duke Ellington, you see, and eventually there he acquired another great act. Of course, Berry Brothers had to go on to Europe, see, so Patterson and Jackson -- they come along. The show got greater and greater. I think someone had to replace

Harry Wills -- he left. He had other commitments, but he really didn't want to go, you know. And -- I think we were somewhere where Ina Ray Hutton was, female band leader. She was -- we didn't believe it, you know. She was in the pit. There was a pit band. I think this was at Tony Pastor's theater, see, and she was a pit band there. During that week that we was there, you see, with Duke Ellington's orchestra and show, he had her to come up on stage and teach us some songs, you know, because she could sing. She was a great singer, Ina Ray Hutton, good Lord, (unintelligible) because -- and then -- she was a favorite, you see, of other musicians, regardless of who they were, whatever, you know. And he had her sing. She sang that song 'Old Shanty Town' -- she sang that.
So, what exactly is sacko? I mean, what physically do they do?
Well, tumbling, I know that. They were tumblers also and that made it sacko because, see, they could come from any -- off the bandstand, or something like that, over one of the -- you know --
No. Tap dancing -- they were jazz tap dancers. The Mao Brothers.
Well, maybe we should clear out the room and have you do some sacko?
See, I like to could do that, you see.
